label: type:decision
title: Decision: identity of the reimplementation and invented identifiers

contextKeys: menu-gating context key (name in spec section 5, step 6)
other: identity card (name, icon, keywords, MIT licence)

notes: Fixes ids, identity card and package properties; defines activation-time detection of the reference extension and full stand-down (nothing registered, gating key false). Much of the content is manifest data, not logic. Core UI surfaces (Issue Reporter, trust prompt) are only verified.
questions: Which context key name gates menus after stand-down, and which libraries own the stand-down step across all family extensions (lib-standdown vs lib-identifiers)?
Is the R-54 warning text and its Manage Extension action specified per extension or shared, so it can live in one library?
Do the invented identifiers table in section 6 and the F-5902 ids form the complete list lib-identifiers must export?

label: type:decision
title: Decision: interface between Remote Explorer and its family companions

other: interface version field in every payload (major.minor)
parallel build of calls, first call getActiveSshRemote
companion interface document copied into both repos
companion absent detection, group appears within 10 s

notes: Defines the cross-extension command contract: who serves, who calls, versioned plain-data payloads, 10 s timeouts, parallel builds, pull-authoritative marker, push wake-up, change signal. Payload fields are provisional until remote-ssh observes them. Candidate for a shared typed client plus server-side registration helper.
questions: What are the exact payload field names and the version field name? The spec defers them to a companion interface document.
Which repository owns the interface document, given it is copied identically into remote-explorer, remote-ssh and remote-server?
Should lib-companion also provide the 10 s timeout, version-mismatch handling and absent-companion detection, or does each view keep its own?
